transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a month after your operation.

So gentle gardening like light weeding or pottering about is fine after that first week, but avoid anything too demanding.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information. Yes, I have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you can go ahead and use your eye gel as you normally would. Just make sure you're storing it as directed on the bottle - some need to be kept in the fridge and others at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for clearing that up. Yes, I do have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please get in touch with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome. Is the light sensitivity mild, or is it quite severe? And is your eye red or painful at all?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's more on the mild side, and it's not painful or red. Just a bit more sensitive than usual.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to hear. In that case, it's nothing to worry about - it's just your eyes adjusting. We'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside, and that should help.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How many days or weeks have passed since your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about a week and a half since my surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
At a week and a half, some mild blurriness can still be normal as your eyes continue to settle. However, if your vision is getting significantly worse or remains quite blurry, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Keep an eye on it over the next few days - it should continue to improve. If you're concerned, let us know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that was my last question. Thank you for all the information, Dora. I really appreciate it!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! Before we finish, can I just confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and remember to wear those sunglasses outside!
